sections.content: How many people are "production managers and directors in construction"?

301,660 people

were counted on the census as "production managers and directors in construction" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Production managers and directors in construction direct and co-ordinate resources for the construction and maintenance of civil and structural engineering works. These projects may include houses, flats, factories, roads and runways, bridges, tunnels and railway works, harbour, dock and marine works and water supply, drainage and sewage works.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "production managers and directors in construction" there were more men than women (87.4% compared with 12.6%).

This means "production managers and directors in construction" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 87.4% and women made up 12.6% of "production managers and directors in construction"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "production managers and directors in construction" included:

  • air transport operatives
  • paper and wood machine operatives
  • energy plant operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "production managers and directors in construction", 15.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "production managers and directors in construction" was 16 to 19 years.

  • production managers and directors in manufacturing
  • higher education teaching professionals
  • residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors

We can look at who worked as "production managers and directors in construction" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "production managers and directors in construction" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "production managers and directors in construction", 7.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (85.3% compared with 14.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (62.2%) than self-employed (37.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
